ocr.notes: Headline garbled and some words lost, but the round-by-round account and names are mostly readable.

title.suggested: Goss wins on a foul over Allen near Walton, Kentucky

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Evening Dispatch reported that militia stopped the Allen-Goss fight after seven rounds, and that Goss was awarded the fight on a foul in the 21st round at a second ring in Boone County, Kentucky.

metadata.notes: Database says Post-Dispatch; the paper was the St. Louis Dispatch in September 1876, before the 1878 merger.

facts.fact: Allen fought Joe Goss near Walton, Kentucky, about 18 miles from Cincinnati; the Covington Light Guards stopped the fight after seven rounds
The fight resumed in a second ring in Boone County and Goss was awarded the fight on a foul in the 21st round for striking Goss on his knees, after 1 hour 52 minutes
Allen came to the grounds with seconds including Tom Kelly, and the fight was refereed by Eph Holland
Allen was arrested when two trains from the fight reached Newport, Kentucky

notes: Foul in the 21st round was claimed by Goss and allowed; Goss was badly beaten.
